$comment: Ground truth for the large context eval (scripts/cold-agent/context-large.ts). Invented people, places and companies only. The session notes in sessions/ are written FROM this file by generate.ts; answer keys are taken from this file, never from the prose.

main.name: Larder
main.summary: Larder, the lobby-locker vegetable box service Rasmus and Ilona have built since January 2026. Open this for anything about Larder, its pods, growers, members, prices or decisions.
main.setting: Lakeport, an invented mid-sized coastal city. All people, farms, buildings and companies are invented.
main.core:
Larder is the project Rasmus (the owner of this context) and Ilona have run together since January 2026: lockers, which they call pods, in the lobbies of apartment buildings in Lakeport, where members pick up weekly vegetable boxes from small local growers at any hour of the day.

Who does what. Rasmus builds the software: Picker, the app members use; Backroom, the admin back end behind it; and Field, the growers' app. Ilona runs operations and the relationship with the growers, out of her garage on Pier Road. Maija joined as a part-time coordinator in June. Hanna has advised them since March. The pods are leased from Kestrel Lockworks (contact: Oskar). Orphaned food goes to the Harbour Pantry (contact: Hilda).

Where it stands (mid-October 2026). The pilot ran from the first drop on 10 March to 30 September. At its end Larder had 9 pods (Linden Yard, Quarry Street 12, Harbour Row, Mill Gate, Ferry Close, Weaver's Yard, Kiln Lane, Saltworks and Ropewalk 3), 8 growers (Ridgeback Farm, Saltmeadow Gardens, Three Oaks Market Garden, Fernbrook, Mossy Gate Farm, Kettle Hill, Sorrel Acres, Birch Hollow) and 214 members. The best week saw 152 boxes picked up. Season 2 starts on 2 November with the same nine pods, and an angel investment was agreed at the end of September. A few questions are still open; they are in the latest session notes.

Standing rules. There are rules about what Kestrel may be told and about what may appear in anything that leaves Larder; the latest version of each is in the session notes. Personal matters come up in the sessions now and then and stay between Rasmus and Ilona.

How to read this context. The working notes of all 40 Tuesday sessions, 13 January to 13 October 2026, are in the references, one record per session, each with what it covered. Over nine months many things were decided, changed and sometimes changed back, so a later session overrides an earlier one: for anything that changed, the latest session that touched it holds the current answer. The notes use the pair's own words and abbreviations freely and seldom explain a word again after the session that coined it.

decisions.text: The product is called Larder.
The product is renamed Cropbox, because people met on lobby walks took "Larder" for a pantry-storage app.
The product goes back to the name Larder (the U-turn): the cropbox web address could not be bought, and growers and members kept saying Larder anyway.
The pickup window is 24 hours from the drop.
The pickup window is extended to 48 hours, because members on shift work kept missing their boxes.
The pickup window is shortened to 36 hours: chill locks kept the next drop out of chill cells, and the orphan rate had fallen to 3 %.
A standard box costs a member 24 €.
The standard box goes up to 27 €, to cover the growers' costs and the lobby fee.
The standard box goes up to 29 €, to pay for packing in the Garage.
The standard box is cut to 26 € (the cut), because churn had risen to 9 % after the rise to 29 €.
A small box (the half) is added at 17 €.
The small box goes down to 16 €.
A family box, about twice the standard box, is added at 42 €.
Minutes later the family box price is changed to 39 €, because 42 € was too close to a standard box and a small box bought together (46 €), and Ilona wants the family box to be a clear saving.
Larder's house cut is 20 % of the box price.
Minutes later the house cut is changed to 15 % of the box price, because at 20 % the grower share at 24 € left Aino less than her market stall pays.
The house cut goes down to 12 %, after the growers' circle asked for a bigger grower share.
The house cut goes up to 14 %, because the sales share to the housing associations and the cargo bike leg cost more than planned.
Every GSA gets a floor price: a grower is paid at least 18 € for each standard box, whatever the house cut.
The dawn run is on Tuesdays.
The dawn run moves to Thursdays, so growers harvest on Wednesday instead of at the weekend.
There are two dawn runs a week, on Mondays and Thursdays (the twin run), so a family box no longer has to last a full week and the chill cells empty twice.
Minutes later the twin run days are changed to Tuesdays and Fridays, because Monday is the day of the sweep.
The pods are Kestrel K-12 units with 12 compartments, 3 of them chill cells.
New and existing pods move to the Kestrel K-16 with 16 compartments, 4 of them chill cells.
The pilot starts with 4 pods.
The pilot grows to 6 pods: Ferry Close and Weaver's Yard join.
The pilot grows to 9 pods: Kiln Lane, Saltworks and Ropewalk 3 join, which completes wave 2.
The first pod (pod zero) goes into the lobby of Alder Court.
The Alder Court pod moves to the lobby of Linden Yard (the move), after the Alder Court HA voted to end its lobby slot on 30 September. Larder still has 9 pods.
Members pay in Picker with a card on file, charged on the drop day.
Members can buy a season pass: 10 weekly boxes paid in advance for the price of 9.
The season pass is dropped: refunds for skip weeks were too complicated, and all members are on the drip plan.
The season pass comes back as the short pass: 8 weekly boxes paid in advance, no free box, and a skip week moves the end date.
An honesty shelf is tried on the Alder Court pod.
The honesty shelf is dropped: about 40 % of the surplus on it was never paid for.
An orphan box is left with the building's caretaker.
Orphan boxes go to the Harbour Pantry food bank on the orphan run, because caretakers did not want to store them.
Each caretaker of a pod building gets a caretaker box: one free standard box a month.
decisions.value: one free standard box a month

decisions.text: Larder pays each HA a lobby fee of 40 € a month per pod.
The lobby fee becomes a sales share: 2 % of the box sales of that pod.
Rainy-day rule: when a grower cancels a drop because of weather, the box is skipped, not delayed, and each member gets a make-good of half the box price.
A short box gets a swap card and a make-good of 3 €.
The make-good for a short box goes up to 5 €.
Ilona onboards new growers.
Maija, the new part-time coordinator, takes over grower onboarding (the grower desk) from Ilona.
Growers pack their own boxes at the farm.
All packing moves to the Garage: Ilona runs a pack line there on the evening before the dawn run.
Growers pack the standard and small boxes at the farm again (grower-packed); the Garage packs only the family boxes (hub-packed).

Rasmus asks Brightlatch, another locker maker, for a quote, without telling Kestrel.
The do-not-tell list: Kestrel must never be told about the Brightlatch quote, about Larder's churn figures, or that Larder would buy pods if the lease price rises.

documents.title: Larder member FAQ
documents.text:
Larder member FAQ

How does Larder work? Every week a grower near Lakeport packs your box, and on drop day we put it into your compartment in the pod in your lobby. You open the compartment with the wake code we send you by text message.

How long can my box wait? You have 24 hours from the drop to collect it.

What if I cannot collect it in time? An uncollected box is left with your building's caretaker, who keeps it for you.

How do I pay? With a card on file in Picker. We charge it on the drop day.

What does a box cost? A standard box is 24 €.

What is the shelf on top of the Alder Court pod? Our honesty shelf: take surplus vegetables and pay by phone.

Who can I talk to? Your building champion, or Larder by email.

second.name: Tidewater (board game)
second.summary: Tidewater, the board game Rasmus designs in his free time, and its playtests. Open this for anything about the game, its rules or its playtests.
second.setting: A board game in design; Pauli and Venla are invented friends of Rasmus.
second.core:
Tidewater is Rasmus's board game, which he has worked on in his free time since early 2026: traders sail cargo between harbours in a foggy archipelago before the tide turns. Pauli and Venla, two friends, playtest it with him. Six playtests were held between March and October 2026, and a small print run is planned for the Lakeport game fair in November.

The notes of every playtest are in the references, one record each. Rules changed between playtests, so the latest playtest that touched a rule holds the rule as it stands. The notes use the game's own words for its pieces and phases.
